newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine presidential guessing game stretches on.
newsitem.headline: Philippine presidential guessing game stretches on.

text.p: Philippine politicians gearing up for the 1998 presidential elections will have to wait for at least another week before they know if President Fidel Ramos will be the man they will face at the polls.

The Commission on Elections (Comelec) postponed to next week a decision on whether to act on a petition by a citizens group urging a referendum on changing constitutional rules to allow Ramos to run for a second term.
The poll body's six commissioners and its chairman met for two hours on Thursday and agreed to vote on the issue next week.
Ramos has pledged to step down when his six-year term ends in May 1998 but has also said citizens had a right to seek changes in the 10-year-old constitution.
Ramos is barred from running for re-election under a constitutional provision that limits a president to one term.

Vice-President Joseph Estrada, a front-runner among about a dozen politicians already jockeying for the presidency, on Wednesday accused Ramos of sowing confusion and challenged him to a one-on-one race in next year's polls.
"I have made my position (not to run) consistent but let me also ask, how sure is he that he will be the one on the other side?" Ramos told reporters, reacting to Estrada's dare.
Speculation mounted that Ramos might stand for a second term after a citizens group called Pirma launched a signature campaign to force a referendum on lifting the terms of incumbent officials.
The Supreme Court last month disallowed the campaign but the group, refusing to give up, brought to Comelec the 5.5 million signatures it says it has collected nationwide to back its petition.
